added.question: Which Trojan hero carried his father Anchises on his shoulders out of burning Troy and, according to Virgil, became the ancestor of the Romans?
Which people's honey-sweet fruit made Odysseus' scouts forget all wish to return home, so that he had to drag them back to the ships?
On which fast day, the saddest of the Jewish year, do Jews mourn the destruction of both Temples in Jerusalem and read the Book of Lamentations?
Which crocodile-headed god of ancient Egypt was worshipped in the Faiyum city the Greeks called Crocodilopolis and in the double temple of Kom Ombo?
Which king of Alba Longa, who had deposed his brother Numitor, ordered the newborn Romulus and Remus to be drowned in the Tiber?
Which river of the Greek underworld made the dead forget their earthly lives when they drank from it?
Into which animal did the jealous Hera turn Callisto, the nymph whom Zeus later set among the stars?
To which realm of Norse mythology, ruled by Loki's daughter of the same name, did those go who died of sickness or old age?
Which Norse goddess, the wife of Odin, tricked her husband into granting victory to the "long-bearded" Lombards?
What is the name of Odin's eight-legged horse, which Loki gave birth to in the shape of a mare?
Which legendary kingdom, the homeland of Tristan, is said to have sunk beneath the sea between Land's End and the Isles of Scilly?
Which Cretan princess, abandoned by Theseus on the island of Naxos, did Dionysus make his wife?
What was the name of the sun disc that the pharaoh Akhenaten had worshipped as the sole god of the Egyptian state?
What are the two wolves called to whom Odin gives all the food from his table, since he himself lives on wine alone?
Which planet, the farthest one known to the ancients, is named after the Roman god of sowing, father of Jupiter, whose December festival was the merriest of the Roman year?
What are the seven daughters of the Titan Atlas called, whom Zeus turned into a cluster of stars to save them from the hunter Orion?
